findings.reason: a node following the section literally would land a refusal that breaks the merge path the section tells coordinators to use, and the plan must say how the merge's dry run is exempted and add an arm showing `crew merge --run` still lands an unmerged head.
findings.text: §5 states the refusal unconditionally and offers "or merges it first" as the coordinator's remedy, but `crew merge --run` validates the run through `merge.require_promotable_head` (`reckon/crew/merge.py:157-180`), which calls `promotion.complete_dry_run` (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:895-905`, "the guards are the promotion's own"), reached from `crew_run_commands.py:330-340` via `verify_promotion`; a head-ancestor guard added to the shared check list therefore refuses every `crew merge --run` on an unmerged head before `land_merge` builds the merge, so the remedy §5 names stops working and no arm in §5's done-when exercises that caller

findings.reason: the ref choice decides whether the guard closes the defect or only one of its two routes, and the section must name it (and whether a fetch is read) for the negative control to be a control over the delivered behaviour.
findings.text: the Deliverable says "not an ancestor of the primary branch" but names no ref, and the done-when's positive arm ("a head already on the branch promotes as before") is satisfied by either reading, while the repo holds both conventions (`merge._is_ancestor(repository, head, "HEAD")` for local `main` at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:327`, versus the remote-tracking primary ref helper at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:944`); a local-`HEAD` test passes a head that `land_merge` fast-forwarded locally and then failed to push (`MergePushOutstandingError`, `reckon/crew/merge.py:808`), which is exactly the "ledger reads landed work that main does not carry" state §5 exists to prevent
